organizations.normalization_notes: The historical territorial-era name is canonical. The archive's University of Hawaiʻi spelling and U.H. are preserved as aliases; the modern repository label is not substituted as the 1942 employer name.
The archival guide identifies the historical organization directly. No modern successor or headquarters location is inferred.

affiliations.date_precision: The archival guide says Keesing taught summer school in 1934 and remained in the Anthropology Department. It identifies him as department chair for 1939/40 and 1940/41, the only full professor in 1941/42, absent from the next faculty listing, and explicitly says he left for OSS in 1942.
affiliations.research_notes: The University of Hawaiʻi is both the explicitly documented immediate pre-OSS affiliation and the last documented civilian employer. The 1941/42 role is professor, not department chair.

affiliations.role_title: Director of research in the Pacific dependencies
affiliations.date_precision: The University of Hawaiʻi archival guide reports that a March 1934 university newspaper article described Keesing as having served in this role before joining the summer-school faculty. Exact start and end dates are not supplied.
affiliations.research_notes: This is an earlier documented pre-OSS employer, not the immediate predecessor to OSS service.

claims.claim_text: The Felix M. Keesing indexed in OSS personnel Box 395 is the University of Hawaiʻi anthropologist whom the university archives document as leaving for OSS in 1942.
claims.evidence_paraphrase: The distinctive exact indexed name and middle initial align with the university archive's full name, anthropology career, and explicit OSS transition.
claims.identity_match_assessment: High confidence from the distinctive exact name and middle initial plus an authoritative institutional chronology that explicitly names his 1942 move to OSS.
claims.temporal_assessment: The index establishes an OSS personnel file; the university archive explicitly places the OSS transition in 1942.
claims.match_notes: The identity does not rely on fame or name recognition alone; the accepted archival source supplies the same person, profession, institution, and OSS chronology.

claims.claim_text: Felix M. Keesing's immediate documented pre-OSS affiliation was his professorship at the University of Hawaiʻi.
claims.evidence_excerpt: left the University of Hawaiʻi for the Office of Strategic Services in Washington, D.C.
claims.evidence_paraphrase: The university archive traces his faculty service through 1941/42 and explicitly states that he left the university for OSS in 1942.
claims.identity_match_assessment: High confidence from the exact distinctive name, middle initial, profession, institutional chronology, and explicit OSS identification.
claims.temporal_assessment: Explicit immediate: the institutional archive directly describes a University of Hawaiʻi-to-OSS transition in 1942.
claims.match_notes: This university employment is also the last documented civilian employer before OSS. The concurrent Columbia wartime teaching association began at the time of the OSS move and is not recast as a pre-OSS employer.

claims.claim_text: The University of Hawaiʻi was Felix M. Keesing's last documented civilian employer before OSS service.
claims.evidence_paraphrase: University catalogs summarized by the archive place him on the faculty through 1941/42, and the archival guide directly links his 1942 departure to OSS.
claims.identity_match_assessment: High confidence from the distinctive exact name and the university archive's continuous faculty and OSS chronology.
claims.temporal_assessment: Explicit immediate transition from university employment to OSS in 1942.
claims.match_notes: The claim identifies a named employer and role. It does not infer employment from education or from his later Stanford career.

claims.claim_text: Before joining the University of Hawaiʻi faculty in 1934, Felix M. Keesing served as director of research in the Pacific dependencies for the Institute of Pacific Relations.
claims.evidence_paraphrase: The university archive reports that a March 1934 university newspaper article identified Keesing's earlier Institute of Pacific Relations research-director role.
claims.identity_match_assessment: High confidence because the role appears within the same institutional biographical chronology that identifies his full name, academic specialty, and later OSS transition.
claims.temporal_assessment: Documented prewar employment before his 1934 University of Hawaiʻi appointment; the source does not establish exact employment dates.
claims.match_notes: This is retained as earlier documented pre-OSS employment and is not labeled immediate.

research_attempts.query_text: Felix M Keesing Office of Strategic Services University of Hawaii pre-OSS employer institutional archives
research_attempts.rejection_reasons: Wikipedia and mirrored biographies were discovery-only; a modern scholarly paper discussed wartime anthropology but did not establish Keesing's employer transition; general Stanford pages documented the repository but not the pre-OSS chronology. Accepted claims rely on the NARA index and the University of Hawaiʻi archival guide.
research_attempts.research_notes: The review resolves the identity at high confidence and identifies the University of Hawaiʻi as both the explicitly immediate pre-OSS affiliation and the last documented civilian employer. The earlier Institute of Pacific Relations role is stored separately as documented prewar employment. Stanford is not treated as pre-OSS because the archive dates that appointment to 1943.
research_attempts.next_action: Review Box 395 for exact OSS entry date, position, assignments, and concurrent Columbia teaching chronology.
